answer: The workshop keeps the velvet, the ledger keeps the quill, time itself keeps the relic — and none of the three works for the farm. Let every applicant face the same trial with Cloisonne engraver ivory enamel roundel warrant enamelled onto the enamel press, and let the answer read as each ivory enamel roundel is a year of enamel logs in the kiln ledger. Time is the toll no farm can skip: 10 minutes per proof, 1460 minutes for 146, due every single epoch. The kiln keeps its own log, the maker keeps the receipt, and any stranger can match the two.
